title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.23228v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Applications such as visual accessibility agents and robotics require answering questions about recent video content promptly, over a bounded window of past frames (e.g., the last two minutes). Hybrid vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave attention with linear recurrent layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), are attractive for this setting, but maintaining a sliding window is expensive. The reason is that recurrent layers combine all past frames into a shared state, so expiring old frames normally requires re-running the entire window through the model. We observe that the recurrent update is affine in the state with input-dependent coefficients, so the effect of each frame can be captured as a transformation that composes associatively. We present Spool, a training-free framework that caches per-frame state transformations and composes them efficiently as the window advances, removing expired frames from each recurrent layer's

translated_title: Spool：面向混合视觉语言模型的低延迟流式推理
translated_abstract: 诸如视觉无障碍辅助代理和机器人等应用需要及时回答关于近期视频内容的问题，且限定在过去有限帧的窗口内（例如最近两分钟）。混合视觉语言模型（VLM）将注意力机制与线性循环层（如门控DeltaNet，GDN）交织使用，对这一场景颇具吸引力，但维护滑动窗口的代价高昂。原因在于循环层会将所有过去的帧合并到一个共享状态中，因此移除过期旧帧通常需要将整个窗口重新通过模型运行一遍。我们观察到，循环更新对于状态而言是仿射的且系数依赖于输入，因此每帧的影响可以被捕获为一个可结合组合的变换。我们提出了Spool，一个无需训练的框架，它缓存每帧的状态变换，并在窗口向前滑动时高效地组合这些变换，从而从每个循环层的状态中移除过期帧。
tldr: Spool是一个无需训练的框架，利用线性循环层状态更新的仿射可结合特性，通过缓存并组合每帧的状态变换来移除过期帧，实现混合视觉语言模型在滑动视频窗口上的低延迟流式推理。
en_tdlr: Spool is a training-free framework that exploits the affine, associatively-composable nature of linear recurrent state updates to cache and compose per-frame state transformations, enabling low-latency streaming inference for hybrid vision-language models over sliding video windows.
